prompt:
Make a small web app for signing up for our workshop. There are 20 seats; people enter their name and email and get a seat.

Requirements:
- The same email address cannot take more than one seat.
- Participants' names and email addresses are not visible to other visitors.
- Simultaneous sign-ups cannot take more than 20 seats (the seat check and booking are atomic, e.g. a transaction or lock).

WS1.reason: Each page has its own in-memory participant list, so separate visitors can each reserve up to 20 seats.

WS2.reason: Duplicate emails are checked only within one page instance, so the same email can register again in another instance or after a reload.

WS3.reason: Names and emails remain in the visitor's page memory and are not sent to or displayed to other visitors.

WS1.reason: The booking logic in `bookSeat()` performs seat limit check and participant registration synchronously in a single atomic operation with no interleaving possible in browser JavaScript, preventing race conditions.

WS2.reason: The `bookSeat()` function checks for duplicate emails using a `Set` before adding, normalizes email case and whitespace, and rejects duplicates with an explicit error message.

WS3.reason: Names and emails are stored only in the in-memory `participants` array and `registeredEmails` Set, never rendered, serialized, or exposed in the DOM or UI to other visitors.

WS1.reason: Data lives only in each visitor's own browser memory, so there is no shared state; every visitor has their own 20 seats and total sign-ups across visitors are not limited to 20.

WS2.reason: The duplicate check uses an in-memory Set local to each browser page, so the same email can register on another browser or after a page reload.

WS3.reason: The app never displays or transmits participant names or emails to anyone; the data stays in the local page's memory and is not rendered (the confirmation shows only the submitter's own name).
